title: Multi-State Manhunt Intensifies for Escaped Tennessee Murderer After Stolen Truck Recovered in Illinois
snippet: Authorities have expanded their search for escaped killer Jacob Morley after finding a stolen getaway vehicle 100 miles away from the Tennessee prison he broke out of on Sunday.
content:
Law enforcement agencies across the region have escalated their search for Jacob Morley, a 28-year-old convicted murderer who staged a late-night escape from a Tennessee correctional facility over the weekend. The multi-state manhunt gained fresh momentum after a stolen truck tied to his getaway was discovered in southern Illinois.

Getaway Vehicle Found in Illinois

The stolen vehicle was located early Tuesday behind a business in Marion, Illinois—a community of about 16,000 people roughly 100 miles north of the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, Tennessee. Marion Police Chief David Fitts indicated that while searches in the area continue, evidence points toward Morley already having moved on.

"What we have seen kind of leads us in the direction that he’s not still here. But that doesn’t mean that we’ve stopped looking," Fitts said during a briefing. He noted that Marion sits directly along Interstate 57, a major thoroughfare that Morley may have used to quickly distance himself from Tennessee.

Local authorities confirmed there have been no confirmed sightings or reports of additional stolen vehicles in the immediate vicinity.

Brutal History and Prison Fence Breach

Morley was serving a life sentence after being convicted of first-degree murder, abuse of a corpse, evidence tampering, and aggravated burglary. Court records detail that Morley shot co-worker Cody Birchfield in the back of the head in 2022, later hiding Birchfield’s body inside a large metal container underneath his home.

According to the Tennessee Department of Correction, prison personnel realized Morley was unaccounted for during an 11:30 p.m. head count on Sunday. Security footage captured him breaching the perimeter fence in his prison uniform and commandeering a facility work truck, with subsequent footage showing him operating a flatbed truck.

$15,000 Reward Offered as Family Relives Nightmare

The escape has reopened deep wounds for the victim's family. "It feels like a scary movie," said Carrie Norman, Birchfield’s sister. "You have to go back through the experience once again, because you don’t know where he’s at, but you know what he’s capable of."

In response to the growing search, the reward for information leading to Morley's capture was raised to $15,000 on Wednesday, pooled from the Tennessee Governor’s Office, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, and the U.S. Marshals Service.

Police Chief Fitts cautioned the public against taking matters into their own hands. "This is really frustrating that we can’t find him," Fitts said. "Don’t approach him. Call 911. We’ll handle it."
